newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end down on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end down on profit-taking.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended mostly down on Thursday on profit-taking despite overnight gains on the London Metal Exchange (LME), traders said.
The most active July 1997 contract ended at an intraday low of 23,900 yuan ($2,879) per tonne, losing 100 yuan. It opened at 24,000 and hit a high of 24,060 yuan per tonne.
April fell 70 to 23,460, May 40 to 23,580, June 40 to 23,780, August 20 to 23,970 and Setember rose 10 to 23,910 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume fell to 22,690 tonnes from 24,610 tonnes.
Copper opened higher on LME gains but profit-taking pushed prices down to end at or near their intraday lows.
Traders said investors were wary about future market trend and most preferred to liquidate their positions at high levels.

"Despite overnight LME gains, investors were eager to offset their long positions with the market likely to consolidate in the short term," one trader said. "There were also lots of speculative funds leaving for the active stock market," he added.
Traders said copper would continue to consolidate in the short term.
"Copper is unlikely to see any sharp gains or falls given the fact that there is no market-moving news," a second trader said.
Aluminium ended mostly down. April fell 20 to 16,000 yuan ($1,928) per tonne, May rose 30 to 16,280, June fell 30 to 16,500 and July was down 100 to 16,600 yuan.
Combined volume rose to 2,370 tonnes from 1,580 tonnes.
